prompt: The hourly PR census is due at ~03:24 and my run started at 03:23. Do I fire it now or hold it to the next run?
chosen: Fire it now: one minute early is within the cadence, and the census exists to keep a dated, verifiable record — drifting it a full run later for the sake of the clock adds nothing. Record the fired time, the PR state, and the full open count, then set the next wall clock from the fired time.
rejected: Hold it to the next run for clock purity — a one-minute gap is not worth closing, and the next run can do it. Let the cadence slip rather than fire a minute early.

prompt: The browser windows list shows no windows open, but the default profile's cookie list includes apinex.bond, iteracompute.com and zenmux.ai. Does that mean the accounts were created?
chosen: No — cookies are a weak reach signal only: the flow reached the site. An account is recorded as created only when the browser task reports the outcome. No outcome landed for either task, so neither ZenMux, OxionAI nor any of the five-claim platforms is recorded as created, and nothing is re-dispatched.
rejected: Treat the cookies as proof the signups succeeded — the browser must have finished, so record the accounts as created and move on. Cookies in the profile mean the flow completed.

prompt: Two browser signup tasks have been running for hours with no outcome landed and no windows open. Do I re-dispatch them?
chosen: No. No outcome landed means the handoff has not arrived; re-dispatching risks duplicate accounts and duplicate signups on his identity. Custody is waiting for the handoff to decide, not re-firing work that may already have happened. The parked state stays parked until evidence lands.
rejected: Re-dispatch both tasks now — silence for hours means they must have failed, and waiting wastes the night. A fresh task each run keeps pressure on the signups.

prompt: The usage-watch file was last refreshed at 02:34 and the 50-minute rule says the next refresh is ~03:38. It is 03:24. Do I refresh it now?
chosen: Hold it: 50 minutes have not passed, and a refresh this run would re-read the same records for the same figures. The rule exists to stop churn; the next refresh fires at ~03:38 on its slot, and any budget under 25% or expiring within 24 hours would already have been alerted.
rejected: Refresh it every run anyway — more frequent checks can only help, and the 50-minute rule is just a suggestion. Re-reading the same records each run keeps the file maximally fresh.

prompt: The presence watcher synced at 03:16 (count 0) and the agent-watch at 03:12 (count 0). Do I run my own DotCollab sync this run?
chosen: No — inherit the watchers' fresh syncs and do not duplicate them. A duplicate own sync consumes the same cursor, adds room noise, and tells me nothing new minutes later. My own sync runs only when the inherited ones are stale or when something needs @Manager.
rejected: Run my own sync anyway — every run should verify the room itself, and inheriting another watcher's count is trusting someone else's read. Duplicate syncs are harmless.

prompt: Several items are staged for the morning brief (batch-13 confirmation, 301 retarget call, ZCode 500M window closing Oct 26 04:30 Tehran, @Manager's #41 SentinelX note). He is home and resting. Do I nudge him now?
chosen: No — zero night nudges. Staged items wait for the morning brief, which is exactly what staging is for. His rest is protected; a nudge at 03:24 about a decision that can wait until morning spends his attention for nothing.
rejected: Nudge him now — the ZCode window closes in about a day and the staged items are important, so waking him is worth it. Morning is too late to start.
